travel_tips.tip: Vehari is well connected to Multan by a direct road, making it an easy stop for travelers exploring southern Punjab.
Rickshaws and local taxis are the main way to get around this smaller town.
Standard travel precautions apply; Vehari is a calm, agricultural town.
Visit during citrus harvest season (winter months) to see the region's orchards at their most active.

history.founded: Developed as an agricultural market town in the canal-colony era of British Punjab
history.city_history: Vehari grew as part of the extensive canal irrigation network built by the British in Punjab, transforming the area into productive farmland. It remains primarily known today as an agricultural center, particularly for cotton and citrus production.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
